correctness.rationale: For c>=3 and k>=3, derive cardinality EJR-1 iff s+x_i>=L=min(k,floor(c)) for each voter; s=2 is excluded. For s=0, cost EJR-1 is equivalent to max(x_i)>c; integer budget and group quotas force the half-integer chamber and x=(floor(c),floor(c)+1). For s=1, cost EJR-1 follows from the cardinality lower bounds, leaving x_i>=L-1 and x1+x2<=c; feasible exactly in the high-cost regime. Binomial subset counts yield all three high-cost plateaus and the fractional chamber. For c<3 or k<=2, selecting both shared projects is a direct witness. Exact direct exhaustive tests cover 72 rational cells and five more k=6 cells.

value.rationale: The initiating research highlights a practical modeling conflict between spending-based and project-count-based representation. This complete controlled phase diagram shows that coexistence can turn off at an integer cost, reappear at the half-integer, and fail again, before a distinct high-cost recovery; it also counts all feasible joint outcomes exactly. The dependence on strict EJR-1 inequalities and discrete project counts supplies substantive structural information rather than just reducing the size of the original witness.
